blocking.section: Decision outcome (ruralz-control and ruralz row); Confirmation (Review checklist item); Figure 1 (node val)
blocking.issue: Partly resolved. The parser and normalization packages are now in the set, but the revision adds `engine/plan` to Ruralz Control and the CLI for supergraph planning checks and also forbids "datasource transports". In v2, federation planning is not in `engine/plan` alone. The research lists `engine/datasource/graphql_datasource` as the federation-aware package, and the planner needs a datasource planner from that package to plan entity fetches. That package also holds the subgraph HTTP and WebSocket client code, so importing it brings in the transports and their modules, including gorilla/websocket. The row leaves this to a spike ('planning without transports') and gives no fallback. The Review checklist then hard-codes a package set without `graphql_datasource`, so the likely spike result would need an amendment to this ADR. The set now also matches neither the tech stack catalog row (`ast` and `astvalidation`) nor its Figure 2 ('parser and validation'). Yet the Proposed amendment asks tech stack to align with 'its own Figure 2 and this package set', and those two disagree.
blocking.evidence: ADR row: "| `ruralz-control`, `ruralz` | The lexer, parser, normalization and validation packages, plus `engine/plan` for supergraph planning checks only; never `engine/resolve`, datasource transports or `subscription` (spike: planning without transports), so planning errors appear in `ruralz bundle validate` |". Checklist: "imports into `ruralz-control` or `ruralz` anything beyond the lexer, parser, normalization and validation packages and `engine/plan`, MUST amend this ADR". Research go-libraries-protocols.md section 1: "`engine/datasource/graphql_datasource` (federation-aware)". Tech stack catalog: "Ruralz Control and CLI import only `ast` and `astvalidation`"; tech stack Figure 2: `gqlv["graphql-go-tools parser and validation"]`. More information: "align its GraphQL catalog row with its own Figure 2 and this package set".
blocking.fix: Decide the package set and give the spike a fallback. Rewrite the row as: "The lexer, parser, normalization and validation packages, plus `engine/plan` and the `graphql_datasource` planner for supergraph planning checks, built with no HTTP or subscription client; never `engine/resolve` or `subscription`. A spike confirms that planning runs without a client. If it does not, supergraph planning errors surface as Node NACKs under option (b) of OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-22, and Ruralz Control and the CLI keep only lexer, parser, normalization and validation." Use the same set in the Review checklist item, the Figure 1 node `val` and the depguard amendment. Extend the G1/G3/license Confirmation bullet to Ruralz Control's and the CLI's linked sets as well. Reword the tech stack amendment to 'align its GraphQL catalog row and Figure 2 with this package set'.

blocking.section: Decision outcome (Transport, ruralzd and GraphQL upstream seam rows); Figure 1 (edge lim -- pass-through --> leg)
blocking.issue: New regression from the L1-3 fix. The ADR now drops the engine's `subscription` package, and pass-through runs without a schema, so it skips `engine/plan` and `engine/resolve` (Figure 1 sends pass-through from `lim` straight to `leg`). No component opens the upstream side of a pass-through subscription. The GraphQL upstream seam row covers only `graphql_datasource` fetches and subgraph subscription upgrades, and those run only in federation mode, where there is a planned schema. The owning document requires pass-through to forward every operation to one `graphql` Upstream, and requires the Upstream side of a subscription to speak `graphql-transport-ws`. A `graphql-ws` client in pass-through therefore needs its frames translated to `graphql-transport-ws`. As written, pass-through subscriptions have no dialer, no framing and no per-operation upstream socket bound, and nothing says whether one upstream socket per operation or per session carries them.
blocking.evidence: ADR ruralzd row: "never `subscription`, since Ruralz frames client subscriptions". Seam row: "`graphql_datasource` fetches and subgraph subscription upgrades use a Ruralz-supplied `http.Client` per upstream leg". Limits row: "Until a pass-through schema source exists, pass-through expands fragments itself and skips schema validation". Figure 1: `lim -- "pass-through" --> leg`. Owning doc, Engine: "Pass-through mode forwards each operation to one `graphql` Upstream"; Subscriptions: "Clients subscribe over WebSocket (`graphql-transport-ws` or `graphql-ws`) or SSE ... subgraphs get `graphql-transport-ws`".
blocking.fix: Add a Rules row: "| Pass-through upstream | Queries and mutations go to the Upstream as an ordinary HTTP upstream leg. Each admitted `subscribe` opens its own `graphql-transport-ws` operation over a coder/websocket client in the `internal/` wrapper, dialed per upstream leg through the same Ruralz `http.Client` (so `onUpstreamRequest` runs per subscription). The wrapper translates `graphql-ws` client frames and holds each event under the 1 MiB chunk cap (target); upstream socket sharing within a session is OQ-multi-protocol-12 | Planned (M3) |". Label the Figure 1 pass-through edge 'pass-through: HTTP leg or wrapper graphql-transport-ws client'. Add a pass-through subscription case, including a `graphql-ws` client, to the protocol conformance suite item in Confirmation.

non_blocking.suggestion: Still open from the previous round: bound the resolver's internal concurrency and goroutines (an engine option or a Ruralz semaphore tied to in-flight units), and say whether query plans are cached per snapshot and bounded by bytes, per 'Bounded everything'.

Say what happens if the spike shows that the engine shares one subgraph WebSocket connection across operations or Consumers, for example through connection deduplication in its subscription client. Name the owner of that setting, so that sharing a connection is not mistaken for sharing a subscription.

The owning document's Engine section credits the engine with 'subscriptions over graphql-ws, graphql-transport-ws and SSE', but this ADR has Ruralz frame the client side. Propose that Multi-protocol state that the engine resolves subscriptions and Ruralz frames them for clients.
State whether pass-through forwards the client's original document or the fragment-expanded one. The answer determines what `onRequestBody` Policies may change and what the Upstream sees.
